thread:
alex: quick check-in — finished 24h bake comparing SmoothQuant + activation-aware (SQ+AA) vs plain AWQ for long-span workloads (48k-120k). posting quick notes, logs attached in thread below.
maria: awesome — high level numbers?
alex: perf: SQ+AA with prefetched KV reduced p99 decode by ~18% on 80k runs vs AWQ-int8 baseline. cost tokens/sec up ~12% (better throughput).
jamal: nice. any accuracy deltas?
alex: small reg in MRR on the long-dialog eval suite: baseline float16=0.0, AWQ-int8=+0.2% (weird), SQ+AA=-0.9% relative to float16. FP8-mix (act-aware FP8, weights int8) had -0.4%.
mar ia: can you drop the exact eval names and numbers? need them for the incident ticket.
alex: eval-suite: longchat-qa-48k (2k queries, average reference len 3). metrics: EM / F1 / MRR. numbers: float16 EM 72.1 / F1 85.3 / MRR 0.912. AWQ-int8 EM 72.3 / F1 85.35 / MRR 0.914. SQ+AA-int8 EM 71.5 / F1 84.6 / MRR 0.903. FP8mix EM 71.9 / F1 84.9 / MRR 0.908.
jamal: interesting that AWQ-int8 slightly beat float16 on MRR. is that noise?
alex: likely within noise but repeated over 3 seeds. AWQ has fewer activation clamp artifacts for this workload. SQ+AA seems to recalibrate activations in ways that hurt rank-sensitive metrics.
dan: did you try applying an automatic fallback policy on tokens where activation norm exceeds X?
alex: yes — did a soft-fallback: if layer_act_norm > 5e2 then use fp16 for that layer for that batch. results: MRR recovered to -0.2% for SQ+AA with fallback, p99 latency increased +4% compared to pure SQ+AA but still better than AWQ baseline.
sylvia: what's the implementation? is it per-layer per-step or only at kv-prefetch boundaries?
alex: per-layer per-batch. cheap check on max(abs(activation)) after quant step. code snippet:```python
if max_abs_act > act_thresh:
    use_fp16(layer)
else:
    quantize_layer(layer, scheme="sq+aa")
```
eval-bot: ran longchat-qa-48k seed3 with fallback policy act_thresh=500 -> EM 71.8 / F1 84.95 / MRR 0.909 (close to FP8mix).
jamal: so fallback looks promising. what's the overhead of the check and switching?
alex: check is negligible (~0.2ms per layer). switching induces kernel path swap which adds ~3-6ms per token when triggered; in our sample it triggered on ~4% of tokens overall.
mar ia: for production rollout we should quantify tail behaviors. can we get a per-segment breakdown by position (first 1k, 1k-10k, 10k-80k)?
jamal: will run stratified runs. also want to test kv-prefetch aggressiveness. We saw prefetch reduced p99 but increased occurrence of act spikes at 90k+.
d an: command you used? I want to reproduce locally.
alex: run:```bash
./bench_eval --model redwood-13b-v3 --quant sq+aa --prefetch-kv=aggressive --fallback act_thresh=500 --eval-suite longchat-qa-48k --seed 3
```
infra-bot: snapshot saved to gs://redwood-bakes/2365001234/sq-actaware-prefetch/ (logs + perf traces).
sylvia: can we try a hybrid quant profile: early layers int8-awq, mid layers sq+aa-int8, last 6 layers fp16? might reduce rank impact.
alex: tried that: early AWQ + mid SQ+AA + tail fp16 -> EM 71.95 / F1 85.0 / MRR 0.910, p99 latency sits between AWQ and pure SQ+AA.
jamal: seems like an operational default: hybrid + fallback + moderate prefetch. create a rollout plan with canary that limits to 5% traffic and synthetic longctx tests.
maria: I'll draft an RFC for the rollout and include perf/regression thresholds: no more than -0.5% EM and -0.8% MRR vs float16 on longchat-qa, p99 <= AWQ+2ms.
alex: adding a knob for auto-calibrate threshold per-model using short calibration run (5k tokens) to pick act_thresh per-run. preliminary script:```bash
python calibrate_act_thresh.py --model redwood-13b-v3 --samples 5000 --metric mrr --target_drop 0.5
```
eval-bot: queued calibration on the cluster (job 73412).
jamal: thanks — i'll run stratified runs and post results later today. if anyone wants raw traces ping me and i'll share the gs link. :+1:
